builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PhOSv1: Efficient Scaling of Model Sleeping on a Single Server for Autoscaling with GPU-Context Deduplication
summary: PhOSv1 replaces per-engine resident GPU contexts in model-sleeping autoscaling (as in vLLM and SGLang) with a central daemon that deduplicates shared CUDA driver contexts and overlapping kernel binaries via API remoting. It costs a modified serving stack with a centralized GPU-context daemon, adding operational complexity and a potential single point of failure rather than extra GPU memory. It can fail through daemon crashes stalling all engines, API-remoting incompatibility with future CUDA or engine versions, and reduced benefit when models lack overlapping kernels—none of which matters for a single-model, single-GPU deployment.
rationale: The technique targets multi-model MaaS autoscaling on a server, a scenario the reader with one 24 GB GPU and limited budget does not operate, and no public implementation or quantified memory factor is given to enable small-scale adoption.

claims.statement: PhOSv1 replaces per-engine resident GPU contexts in model-sleeping autoscaling (as in vLLM and SGLang) with a central daemon that deduplicates shared CUDA driver contexts and overlapping kernel binaries via API remoting. It costs a modified serving stack with a centralized GPU-context daemon, adding operational complexity and a potential single point of failure rather than extra GPU memory. It can fail through daemon crashes stalling all engines, API-remoting incompatibility with future CUDA or engine versions, and reduced benefit when models lack overlapping kernels—none of which matters for a single-model, single-GPU deployment.
Matches the scale-up time of vanilla vLLM sleep mode while substantially reducing the GPU memory footprint of sleeping models, improving end-to-end multi-model serving performance.
